_meta.description: Age-specific prevalence of diabetes and hypertension, used by cost_of_delay to estimate the chance of developing a condition while waiting to buy cover. Prevalence is in % of adults; each band is placed at its midpoint age and interpolated linearly.
_meta.method: P(develop c during delay | free at age a) = max(0, prev(a + k) - prev(a)) / (1 - prev(a)). Cross-sectional prevalence differences approximate incidence (ignores cohort effects and deaths); conditions are combined assuming independence.

hypertension.source: NCHS Data Brief No. 511 (Oct 2024): hypertension prevalence, August 2021-August 2023

diabetes.source: CDC National Diabetes Statistics Report 2017 release (2015 data): 4% of adults 18-44, 17% of 45-64, 25% of 65+ had diabetes
diabetes.quality: national estimate; older than the hypertension data (2023 overall prevalence is 12.0%)

diabetes.source: Mohamed SF et al., Prevalence and factors associated with pre-diabetes and diabetes mellitus in Kenya: results from a national survey (STEPS 2015), BMC Public Health 2018;18(Suppl 3):1215, Table 3

hypertension.source: Kenya STEPS 2015 survey: hypertension 17.7% at 18-29 and 58.3% at 60-69 (overall 28.6%), as reported in a 2020 secondary analysis of the survey; intermediate bands interpolated
hypertension.quality: secondary report of a national survey; only two bands published in the text read

national.source: Anjana RM et al., Metabolic non-communicable disease health report of India: the ICMR-INDIAB national cross-sectional study (ICMR-INDIAB-17), Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023;11:474-89

age_shape.source: The ICMR-INDIAB-17 main paper gives no age-band table, so India's bands are the US age pattern scaled to India's national prevalence (diabetes x 11.4/12.0, hypertension x 35.5/47.7; US overall: CDC 2023 12.0%, NCHS 2021-23 47.7%). Lower confidence than USA and Kenya.

IND.health: Any condition diagnosed before buying becomes a pre-existing disease: it is excluded for up to 36 months (IRDAI maximum), and insurers may add a premium loading, a co-pay, or decline.
IND.health_source: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, 29 May 2024 (36-month PED maximum)

USA.health: ACA plans cannot refuse cover or charge more for pre-existing conditions, but you can only enrol in open enrolment or after a qualifying life event.
USA.health_source: 45 CFR 147.102 (premium may vary only by age, tobacco, area and family size)

KEN.health: Chronic and pre-existing conditions face a 1-year wait and a sub-limit (Old Mutual AfyaImara: KES 400,000 on the KES 1M option) or a 6-month wait (AAR); a medical report is required above age 45 (AAR) or 60 (Old Mutual).
KEN.health_source: Old Mutual AfyaImara brochure (2022), benefit table; AAR SME brochure (2017), general conditions

consequences.term_life: Term life is medically underwritten in all three countries: diabetes or hypertension can mean a premium loading, a postponement or a decline. The size of a loading varies by insurer and is not modelled.
